scope: Sixteenth expansion batch: 12 controlled tsumori exercises, three each for current affirmative plans, negative plans, past intentions and past beliefs in completed actions. Noun/adjective self-assessment and imagined-role uses are not covered by this batch.

sources.section: The Basics and Verb + tsumori; nai-tsumori; tsumori-datta; ta-tsumori; and Beyond the Basics: tsumori wa/ga nai. Plain verb attachment, short- and long-term plans, a past intention versus a belief in attainment, and past copula placement were inspected. The study example first expresses a belief in adequate preparation without establishing failure, then adds a later failed-test context. The failed-intention scenarios illustrate a frequent use, not a logical assertion that every past intention was unfulfilled.

Main About explanation: dictionary/negative verb forms before tsumori da/desu, and intending not to act versus having no intention of acting. Simplified extraction omitted the inline examples, so those missing examples are not cited. No universal ranking of denial strength, equivalence of all negative endings, or etymological explanation is adopted.

The tsumori noun entry's intention/plan and belief/assumption senses; the separate tsumori-de-aru expression's second sense, with its note that it follows a past-tense verb. These establish lexical uses, not the naturalness of the original scenarios. Tsumori is printed outside every blank, so this batch does not test its spelling variants.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are original. The source patterns do not by themselves attest the new sentences; the batch requires independent editorial review.

The first six questions request only the supplied verb's dictionary or nai form, with tsumori desu already printed. The same verbs (read, buy, use) appear on both sides. The questions distinguish a chosen negative plan from inability, dislike or an indefinite absence of any decision.

The later six questions all print tsumori deshita and request only the supplied verb's dictionary or ta form. Each question also states the requested mental stance before answering. The same verbs (send, close, reserve) appear on both sides, so neither the outer past ending nor the verb itself supplies the answer.

The fulfilled Friday-reservation plan retains the Monday viewpoint. The confirmed-window belief and wrong-room booking prevent a blanket equation of ta-tsumori with a wholly unperformed action or necessarily false belief. The scenarios explicitly supply the actual outcome separately.

The full linked article inventory was screened. Alternative intention, decision, inference and temporal expressions may be natural whole-sentence reformulations; they are not additional literal verb forms to insert before the supplied tsumori. Nai-tsumori and tsumori wa/ga nai can overlap in practical use and are not competing buttons here.

Tofugu and Bunpro describe the force of negative-intention formulations differently in their selected contexts. No universal stronger/weaker rule is used to determine an answer. Likewise, no blanket person restriction, guaranteed plan fulfillment or fixed imminence rule is adopted.

Search suggestions for nihongokyoshi.tufs.ac.jp/lessons/grammar/032.html and www.minna-no-kyouzai.jp/column/nihongo_kyoushi/vol8 failed host resolution and were not evidence. TUFS's actual module index and explanation/066.html were inspected; the latter concerns volitional forms with to omou, not a dedicated tsumori lesson, so it is not attributed as one.

All 209 prior exercises remain unchanged: 197 in the committed baseline and 12 in the separately hashed uncommitted degree/extent file. The prior article is preserved beneath this batch's added subsection and reference. Each new exercise has one stable SRS identity, not separate identities for kana and kanji answers.
